section.title: What the Network Still Watches
section.form_description: Two old friends going back over the campaigns over beers. Warm, unhurried, no case to make — just "remember when." Sections are adventures recalled, and the narration keeps losing the thread onto opinions about lore, culture and how things work, then circling back. Runs everything against the Shepard it remembers — this persona's choices, temper and habits are the yardstick the stories and the digressions get measured by.
section.form_note: Two old friends over drinks, except the beer is on a cliff on Rannoch and the war is the Migrant Fleet's and the Council races' shared one. Tali and Liara alternate turns strictly, 6 each; no voice holds two in a row, since this is exactly the kind of unhurried back-and-forth the form wants. Each turn's first promise is its reply to the one before — Liara picks up Tali's line about the air, Tali corrects Liara's secondhand version of the trial, and so on — and both keep losing the thread onto lore (geth cognition, Thessia, admiralty politics, asari mourning custom) before drifting back to the cliff. The two women never knew Shepard chose Synthesis, and the section list is built so neither has to name it: they talk about what changed after the Crucible fired, not why.

promises: answers Tali directly — she has been to Rannoch before, but always on business, never long enough to sit still; she watched the resettlement mostly through her network, and this is the first evening the two of them have simply had here together
what keeping an intelligence network running in peacetime has cost her, hedged the way she hedges unverified intel
a dry, guarded admission that the habit of watching is also a way of not sitting still with the loss
turns the talk toward what she still doesn't tell anyone, even Tali, about what the network is for now

required_facts.fact: Following the Baria Frontiers bombing on Illium and the death of the traitor Spectre Tela Vasir, Sekat's recovered data pinpoints the Shadow Broker's base: a massive ship riding the eternal storm front of the planet Hagalaz in the Sowilo system. Commander Shepard and Liara T'Soni land on the vessel's hull and fight along its exterior through Shadow Broker agents, engineers, heavies, LOKI mechs and rocket drones, exposed to lightning strikes, before breaching the interior. Inside, they find Feron, Liara's drell partner from the search for Shepard's body, strapped to an interrogation chair wired so that removing him would kill him. They press on to the Broker's command centre and confront the Shadow Broker himself, a hulking yahg, a member of a pre-spaceflight species from Parnack. The Broker reveals he killed and replaced the original Shadow Broker decades earlier and has run the organisation ever since. Shepard and Liara kill him in a heavy firefight. With the Broker dead, Liara seizes control of his information network, assuming the role of the Shadow Broker herself (per `shadow_broker`: the past Broker dies and Liara takes over). Feron is freed from the chair and, mentally scarred from years of torture that he survived using his drell eidetic memory, chooses to stay and assist Liara. Liara begins using the network against the Reapers and the Collectors, and cleans up the Cerberus information leaks that had helped locate the base. Her new resources make her a key intelligence asset for the coming war, and if Shepard is romancing her the relationship is rekindled aboard the captured ship.
The yahg Shadow Broker is killed and his identity and history exposed
Per `shadow_broker`: Liara T'Soni takes over the Shadow Broker organisation and its ship
Feron is rescued and becomes one of Liara's agents, running Terminus operations
Liara gains a galaxy-spanning intelligence network she later turns against the Reapers
Cerberus information leaks that led to the base are shut down
If Shepard did not help take the base, Liara later storms it with mercenaries and Feron does not survive

canon.statement: Shepard was born in Normandie in France, parentless, ran with a gang as a child and had a drug problem before Anderson pulled him into N7.
canon.overrides: Earthborn background as the wiki describes it

canon.statement: In the first weeks after the war, Shepard's death is not confirmed to the crew. Anderson never saw him on the station. The Normandy crash-landed, there's been no word, and the crew takes that silence to mean he's dead: there's no body and no report. After a few months, Shepard is held to be dead by everyone, the crew included: the rubble has been cleared, what the Crucible did is better understood, and there was nowhere on the station he could have escaped to. There is still no body.
canon.overrides: shepard_fate = Dead (synthesis) stated as settled fact

canon.statement: Shepard never had a first name. "Shepard" started as a mocking nickname the Tenth Street Reds gave him for his knack with people. He only took a surname because Alliance enlistment required one, and he kept that one as a screw-you to the Reds.
canon.overrides: Earthborn Shepard as the wiki describes it (first name player-chosen, surname by birth)

canon.statement: Shepard got clean of drugs but never stopped loving alcohol and parties. Jack thinks the good-guy act is just that, an act: in her telling he has turned up at every bar in the galaxy and calls each one his favorite, and he drinks and dances every time. He even did it on Omega, where somebody could have poisoned him. She calls him a drunk and a dumbass, and she's fond of him.
canon.overrides: corpus portrays Shepard's drinking and dancing only in scattered scenes

canon.statement: Jack is teaching Shepard to loosen up when he dances, and she has dragged him into a mosh pit.
canon.overrides: no such relationship beat in the corpus

canon.detail: Like to think that I was born in Normandie, in France, without parents. Joined the gang at a young age, had drugs issues, but Anderson got me out and put me in the N7 program.

Sole survivor of the thresher maw attack on Akuze — his entire squad died, he lived, and the guilt of that day never left him. It's the thing under the bravado: he half-believes he's owed a death he keeps not getting.
Uses Biotic charges and shotguns extensively to kill everyone in sight
Depends on the run. But I stay faithful all trilogy long.

scenes.title: Storming the Broker's Ship and Freeing Feron
scenes.when: 2185, during Lair of the Shadow Broker, after the death of Tela Vasir on Illium
scenes.where: the Shadow Broker's storm-riding ship in the atmosphere of Hagalaz, Sowilo system, Hourglass Nebula

beats.text: Sekat's data placed the Broker aboard a huge ship riding the perpetual storm front of Hagalaz. Shepard, Liara and a third squadmate shuttled down and fought across the ship's exterior against maintenance drones that took them for storm debris, then Broker agents, heavies and mechs, amid discharging lightning capacitors.
At a locked hatch Liara ran a hacking device while the squad held the spot through a long five-wave siege of Shadow Broker forces, including rocket drones, then pushed inside toward the prison block.

They reached Feron, pinned in a restraint rig. Liara tried to free him and only triggered a shock; Feron said pulling him loose would fry his brain, and questions about the Broker shocked him again. Shepard remarked it had been too easy. Shepard and Liara decided to confront the Broker directly.

In his office the Broker waited behind his desk, a giant of a species none of them recognised. If the Collectors were still active, he said his standing offer for Shepard's body held; if they were beaten, he meant to take the Normandy SR-2's Reaper IFF to salvage Collector technology. He dismissed Liara, claiming to know her every secret.

Liara named him: a yahg, taken off his homeworld as a trophy, who had killed the original Shadow Broker and taken his place some sixty years earlier. Enraged, he smashed his desk and hurled it, knocking out the third squadmate. Shepard and Liara fought the yahg through a three-stage battle.
On Liara's cue, Shepard drew the Broker's attention while Liara used her biotics to drop the electrified fluid tank above him. His barrier overloaded and exploded, killing him.

With comms glitching, the Broker's agents called in for orders. Liara answered in the Broker's modulated voice, told them it was a hardware fault, and ordered every operation to report within one solar day. Feron came in with a drawn pistol, then lowered it. Liara said she was now the Shadow Broker. Shepard could hold her as she wept that her two-year hunt was finally over; she granted Shepard permanent access to the base and its network.

variants.text: If Shepard had romanced Liara in Mass Effect, she later met Shepard aboard the Normandy SR-2 and returned Shepard's old dog tags, recovered from the wreck of the Normandy SR-1; they were kept afterwards in the captain's cabin.

evidence.text: The interior of the ship has many compartments including the ship's engines, which must remain active at all times to prevent it from falling. Also inside is central operations, probably the nerve center of the ship. There is also a prison block where the Shadow Broker keeps hostages, and torture facilities for interrogation purposes. Finally there is the Shadow Broker's Office, Intel Center, and private quarters. Within the private quarters, a custom VI Drone assists the Shadow Broker with maintaining his massive network of informants, contacts, and agents. Despite the ship's volatile location, motion dampeners absorb the noise and vibrations from the storm outside.
evidence.for_key: Shadow Broker network operations and information economy

evidence.text: As befits such an influential and well\-funded criminal figure, the Shadow Broker has a private army at their disposal to carry out operations that require the application of force. All Shadow Broker troops wear black and white armor, and bear the Shadow Broker's insignia: a triangular red emblem that strongly resembles a yahg's maw. - Shadow Broker Agent - Shadow Broker Engineer - Shadow Broker Heavy - Shadow Broker Vanguard - Rocket Drone
evidence.for_key: Shadow Broker network operations and information economy

We wouldn't mind helping her in that hunt, given the Broker's past work for the Collectors. We recently uncovered some information that might give Liara a lead on where to find the Shadow Broker's base of operations, but unfortunately, she doesn't have much faith in Cerberus intel. If you'd visit Illium and pass it on to her as a gesture of goodwill, we'd appreciate it. On the Galaxy Map this mission is titled *Give Liara Intel*.

evidence.text:
The Shadow Broker Base was a massive unnamed ship that traveled through the volatile atmosphere of Hagalaz, whose electrical storms concealed its presence. From here the Shadow Broker ran his information empire.

The exterior was hazardous, patrolled by the Broker's private army and tended by Maintenance Drones, with no handrails or guardrails; large conducting rods channeled lightning into hull-mounted capacitors to protect patrols. The interior held the engines, which had to run constantly to keep the ship aloft, a central operations center, a prison block and torture facilities for interrogation, and the Broker's office, Intel Center, and private quarters, where a custom VI Drone helped manage the network of informants and agents. Motion dampeners absorbed the noise and vibration of the storm.

After the yahg Shadow Broker's defeat and Liara T'Soni's ascension as the new Broker, Commander Shepard gained free access to the base, where drones repaired the battle damage over subsequent visits. Veetor's Freedom's Progress footage of the Collector abductions could be seen on screens there. The Intel Center held numerous terminals: Advanced Training (respec a squadmate for 1000 element zero), an Armor Locker, Delivery Pickup (daily shipments of weapon upgrades or randomized resources), Dossiers (intelligence files on the squad and others), the Info Drone, Investment Opportunities, a Research Terminal, a collectible Shadow Broker ship model, shutter and sound-system controls, Survey Information (buy locations of resource-rich planets), and the Video Archive of surveillance clips from across the galaxy.

Sometime before the 2186 Reaper invasion, Liara learned the Illusive Man had tracked her and intended to seize the base for Cerberus. Knowing the aging ship could not travel in space, she and Feron loaded as much information and communications equipment onto a shuttle as they could, escaped, and remotely crashed the base into a Cerberus cruiser, destroying both ships. Assorted tech salvaged from the wreckage was later used to help build the Crucible.

evidence.text: Cerberus attempted to take over the Shadow Broker operations prior to the Reaper invasion of 2186, but Liara opted to crash the Broker's ship into one of their cruisers, only taking the operating necessities with her. She sets up her Broker equipment aboard Miranda Lawson's former quarters in the renovated Normandy SR\-2, resuming eavesdropping operations and directing the flow of her resources for the war. Her network of agents is intact, but the war is taking a toll on their numbers. Some of the Broker's resources are scattered across the galaxy, awaiting discovery. Liara took the Broker's old Info Drone with her, renaming it "Glyph". It is in charge of gleaning useful information from recovered intel in addition to coordinating Liara's massive data feeds. Even during the war, very few people are aware of the Shadow Broker's identity: Liara has made no steps to expose herself. Long\-time underlings like Barla Von are unaware of any change. Urdnot Wrex, if he's alive, may only make snide allusions regarding it. |  | ***“Make no mistake — this is a one\-way trip.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Andromeda** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |
evidence.for_key: Shadow Broker network operations and information economy

evidence.text:
Feron was a drell information trafficker who described himself as "an information trader. Not a slaver." In Mass Effect: Redemption, set after the destruction of the Normandy SR-1, Liara T'Soni hired him to help find Commander Shepard; he reported that Shepard was neither dead nor alive. Ambushed by Blue Suns sent by the Shadow Broker to delay Liara, the pair were saved by an unknown sniper, then encountered Cerberus agents, including Miranda Lawson, and were brought to the Illusive Man, who revealed the Shadow Broker was working with the Collectors. Feron admitted he had been ordered to lead Liara away from Shepard but chose to help her instead.

Feron took Liara to Afterlife on Omega, where Aria T'Loak resided, and learned where the Blue Suns would bring Shepard's body. He spotted the Broker's enforcer Tazzik but missed his ship with a turret, letting Tazzik flee Omega with the body. Feron revealed he had never stopped working for the Shadow Broker, which they could exploit to track Tazzik. The two infiltrated the Broker's base on Alingon, with Feron passing Liara off as his prisoner; he downloaded the Broker's dealings while Liara distracted a hologram of the Broker. Feron confessed Cerberus had recruited him and that he and the Illusive Man had planned for Feron to snatch the body. When a Collector exposed him as a traitor, Feron held off Tazzik so Liara could escape, and was captured.

In Mass Effect 2, Liara mentioned a "friend" lost during her search. During Lair of the Shadow Broker, Liara, Shepard, and Cerberus intel led to the Shadow Broker Base on Hagalaz, where Feron was found being tortured on a device that could not be removed without killing him. Liara and Shepard killed the Shadow Broker; Liara took over the role, and Feron chose to stay and assist her, mentally scarred and using his drell memory recall to survive the torture. In Mass Effect 3, if Shepard helped Liara take the Broker ship, Feron helped evacuate it during a Cerberus attack, became one of Liara's agents controlling Terminus operations (to Tazzik's dismay), and emailed Shepard offering information via Glyph. If Shepard did not help overthrow the Broker, Liara hired mercenaries to storm the lair and Feron did not survive.
evidence.for_key: Shadow Broker network operations and information economy

evidence.text: *Main article: Info Drone* The Info Drone is a specially built VI that assists the Shadow Broker in coordinating the network. It follows the "Broker" around, as it is programmed to recognize anyone in the room as the Broker, and give them periodic updates about the Galaxy and the people in it.
evidence.for_key: Shadow Broker network operations and information economy

evidence.text:
Lair of the Shadow Broker was a Mass Effect 2 mission in which Commander Shepard helped Liara T'Soni track down the Shadow Broker. It became available after the DLC install and the Horizon mission, triggered by a Cerberus message on the Galaxy Map titled "Give Liara Intel," offering intel on the Broker's base because of his past work for the Collectors. The mission ran without a break from Illium to its end and featured mostly shielded enemies.

On Illium, Shepard delivered the intel to Liara in her office; the data also revealed that Feron, Liara's drell partner who sacrificed himself two years earlier, was still alive. Arriving at Liara's apartment, Shepard met the asari Spectre Tela Vasir investigating an assassination attempt on Liara. Clues led to Sekat, an information broker at the Dracon Trade Center, which exploded as the squad arrived. Fighting through the Shadow Broker's private army with Vasir, Shepard found Liara alive; Liara exposed Vasir as a long-time Shadow Broker asset who had killed Sekat and taken his data. Vasir fled, leading to a firefight, a skycar chase through Nos Astra, and a rooftop battle at the Azure hotel that ended with Shepard killing Vasir, who justified her betrayal as the price of intel that saved lives and accused Shepard of hypocrisy for working with Cerberus.

The trail led to the Broker's ship orbiting in the perpetual storm band of Hagalaz. Shepard, with Liara as a mandatory squadmate, fought across the ship's exterior amid lightning capacitors and maintenance drones, defended a door during a long five-wave siege, and pushed inside to free Feron. Confronting the Shadow Broker revealed him to be a yahg, taken from his homeworld and having killed and replaced the original Broker decades earlier. After a three-stage boss fight, Liara dropped an electrified fluid tank to overload his barrier and kill him. Liara assumed the Broker's identity and network, becoming the new Shadow Broker, and granted Shepard permanent access to the base. If Shepard had romanced Liara in Mass Effect, she later returned Shepard's dog tags recovered from the Normandy wreck. Rewards included 90,000 credits, element zero and palladium, and Heavy Pistol Damage and Damage Protection upgrades. Cut content included early plans to rescue Liara from the Broker or to make Shepard the Shadow Broker.
evidence.for_key: Shadow Broker network operations and information economy

evidence.text:
The Shadow Broker was an enigmatic figure at the head of a vast organization that traded in information, always selling to the highest bidder. The Broker balanced its sales so that no client ever gained a decisive advantage, forcing customers to keep trading and keeping the organization in business. The Broker operated only through agents, and its identity was unknown to the public. In 2183 Barla Von called the Broker "he" for convenience but believed it was a group, since no single individual could monitor so much information.

The Broker's dealings touched many events. In 2161 it tasked its associate Brooks to kill Roth, a Cerberus funder, and transfer his funds to Barla Von; Brooks was shot and left for dead, derailing the plan. The Broker also arranged the conspicuous destruction of the turian frigate Verrikan to embarrass the Hierarchy, hiring Zaeed Massani for the job. Tali'Zorah came to the Citadel to trade her evidence that Saren Arterius had gone rogue, routed through the Broker's agent Fist, but Fist had switched allegiance to Saren, so the furious Broker hired Urdnot Wrex to kill him. Admiral Kahoku bought the Broker's services to locate Cerberus, learning only that they were active in the Voyager Cluster. Batarian mercenaries once used the Broker to learn Thane Krios's identity, leading to the murder of his wife Irikah.

After the Normandy SR-1's destruction, the Collectors hired the Broker to retrieve Shepard's body; the Broker sent its enforcer Tazzik, who succeeded despite interference from Liara T'Soni and Feron. Liara and Feron tracked Tazzik to the Broker's base on Alingon, where they found the Broker was communicating through a machine; Feron was captured. Pursuing Feron, Liara eventually teamed with Commander Shepard to raid the Broker's ship on Hagalaz. The Shadow Broker was revealed to be a yahg, a pre-spaceflight species from Parnack; the original Broker had had a yahg abducted for study around 2125, and the captive, operating as "Operative Kechlu," killed and replaced his handler, then pre-empted the Broker's attempt to eliminate him and seized the role, running the organization for about six decades. Having learned of the Reapers and the truth about the Collectors, he had dealt with the Collectors in a bid for his own survival. Shepard and Liara killed the yahg by turning his own kinetic technology against him, and Liara became the new Shadow Broker, taking his Info Drone (renamed "Glyph"). In 2186, facing a Cerberus takeover attempt, Liara crashed the Broker's ship into a Cerberus cruiser and relocated operations aboard the Normandy SR-2. Few knew of the leadership change; the black market only sensed the Broker had "gone soft." An audio log revealed Alec Ryder had reached the Broker through Barla Von for help developing SAM. The Broker's troops wore black-and-white armor bearing a triangular red emblem resembling a yahg's maw, and its forces included Agents, Engineers, Heavies, Vanguards, and Rocket Drones.

evidence.text: *Main article: Lair of the Shadow Broker (mission)* Shepard is sent information on the Shadow Broker obtained by Cerberus. Shepard travels back to Illium and passes this information onto Liara, who examines it and determines that Feron is indeed alive, and in the custody of the Shadow Broker. After surviving an assassination attempt by a rogue Spectre working for the Shadow Broker, Tela Vasir, Liara, with assistance from Shepard and the information obtained from Cerberus, travels to the Shadow Broker Base on the planet Hagalaz. There, they find Feron being tortured for his previous betrayal of the Broker. Unable to remove the drell from the device holding him down without killing him, Liara and Shepard confront the Shadow Broker, killing him in the process. Now free from the Shadow Broker's custody, Feron opts to remain in the Shadow Broker's base so he can assist Liara, who has taken over as Shadow Broker following the previous Broker's death. He remains unsure what he will do afterward. Liara expresses great concern for Feron, worried his ordeal has left him mentally scarred. In conversation with Shepard, he mentions using his drell ability to slip into old memories to escape the torture. Shepard can ask Liara if she is romantically involved with Feron, and her answers will differ slightly depending on whether or not Shepard is in a relationship with Liara, but both result in Liara denying it. However, her response is somewhat ambiguous if Shepard is not romancing Liara. She points out that at this time, Feron is too emotionally unstable for a relationship and that it would be irresponsible "to take advantage" of the situation. Asking Feron about his relationship with Liara will result in him saying that Liara is a far better friend than he deserves. |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |
evidence.for_key: Liara becoming the Shadow Broker on Hagalaz

evidence.text: **Hagalaz** is the *third* planet orbiting the star Sowilo. *Main article: Hagalaz* - *Mission:* Lair of the Shadow Broker (mission)
evidence.for_key: Liara becoming the Shadow Broker on Hagalaz

evidence.text: If Liara succeeded in saving Feron from the Shadow Broker, following the destruction of the Shadow Broker Base in 2186, Liara tasks Feron with tracking Tazzik down. According to Feron, Tazzik is none too pleased to learn that he has to take orders from Feron, but he complies and acts as a bodyguard for Feron and a group of Shadow Broker agents as they travel through the Terminus Systems to gather intel. Tazzik is unaware of Liara's place as the new Shadow Broker and it can be inferred that he assumes that nothing has changed, aside from Feron becoming an asset instead of a liability.
evidence.for_key: Liara becoming the Shadow Broker on Hagalaz

evidence.text: *Main article: Liara T'Soni* Liara T'Soni becomes the Shadow Broker herself and assumes control of his organization regardless of Shepard's involvement. Liara has been trying to sift through the Broker's Reaper\-related files, but quickly finds herself overwhelmed with too much information. Only close contacts such as Admiral Hackett know of the clandestine shift in leadership. However, the Illusive Man has somehow managed to monitor Liara at the Broker's airborne base on Hagalaz. The Broker's behavior has been a subject of scrutiny in some circles. The old Broker, according to the Illusive Man's assessment, kept his subjects in line through fear. In the galactic black market, people are beginning to sense that the Shadow Broker is "going soft." |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |
evidence.for_key: Liara becoming the Shadow Broker on Hagalaz

evidence.text:
Shadow Broker Engineers were the tech specialists of the Shadow Broker's private army, tasked with defending the Broker's interests. They were encountered by Shepard, Liara T'Soni and the squad during the Lair of the Shadow Broker mission, appearing on Illium and at the Broker's base on Hagalaz.

Offensively they carried the M-6 Carnifex and used the Combat Drone and Incinerate abilities. Defensively they had moderate health and shielding plus access to Tech Armor. Recommended tactics were to stay in cover against Incinerate, shoot down their Combat Drones, and use Energy Drain to quickly strip their shields while restoring the player's own.
evidence.for_key: Liara becoming the Shadow Broker on Hagalaz

evidence.text:
Shadow Broker Vanguards were the biotic experts of the Shadow Broker's private army, tasked with defending the Broker's interests. They were encountered by Shepard, Liara T'Soni and the squad during the Lair of the Shadow Broker mission, appearing on Illium and at the Broker's base on Hagalaz.

They were armed with the M-27 Scimitar shotgun and could use Warp. Defensively they had moderate health and barriers bolstered by Tech Armor and Barrier. They typically used Warp to weaken a target before charging in, so the recommended approach was to keep them at range; at melee range, repeated melee attacks could stun-lock them, and Liara's Stasis was highly effective, letting the player finish them quickly once the effect ended.
evidence.for_key: Liara becoming the Shadow Broker on Hagalaz

evidence.text: After the Normandy SR\-1 was destroyed in a surprise attack by the Collector Cruiser and Commander Shepard is killed, the Illusive Man personally coordinates the efforts of Liara T'Soni and Feron to infiltrate the Shadow Broker's organization and prevent the acquisition of Shepard's body by the Collectors. Miranda Lawson, along with several Cerberus troopers, ambushes and kills the Blue Suns mercenaries that detain Liara and Feron on Omega and takes them to a safehouse to introduce Liara to the Illusive Man. The leader of Cerberus persuades her to work for him and use Feron, admitting that his own assets are likely to be ineffective against the Shadow Broker; despite its human\-centric reputation, Cerberus is not above employing and relying on agents of alien species. In the end, Liara and Feron succeeds in their mission, allowing Cerberus to gain intel on the Shadow Broker's operations, as well as acquire Shepard's body so that the Commander could be revived. |  | ***“Salvation comes with a cost.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Ascension** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |
evidence.for_key: Feron and the running of the Broker's agents

evidence.text: Liara once again accuses Feron of purposely holding her back, but gives him one last chance when he says that they can still follow and catch Tazzik using Feron's own ship. Miranda tracks Tazzik from a Cerberus ship as he approaches the Omega 2 Relay. The Illusive Man tells her to stand down; Cerberus already knows where Tazzik is going, and they still need to learn why the Collectors want Shepard. On Feron's ship, Feron informs Liara that the Shadow Broker only has one base on the other side of the mass relay, in the Faryar system on the planet Alingon. Upon arriving in\-system, Feron's ship is attacked by the Shadow Broker's sentries. As Feron's ship isn't armed, he flies through a nearby mined\-out asteroid to evade the sentries, which crash one by one. On Alingon's surface, Feron and Liara make their way to the Shadow Broker's base. Because of Alingon's strong electromagnetic field, only the most sophisticated communications technology is functional; the Shadow Broker is the only one with such technology, which forces his agents to come personally to Alingon to confer with him and make any calls on his behalf only while offworld. Feron charms his way past the base's turian guards, convincing them Liara is a prisoner. Upon spotting a Collector on its way to meet Tazzik's ship, Liara wants to find Shepard immediately. Feron persuades her to wait so they can find out why the Collectors want Shepard in the first place. Feron takes Liara to the Shadow Broker's inner sanctum, where all of his agents receive their orders. There, the obscured figure of the Shadow Broker reacts with surprise to Feron's arrival, and surmises he was right in sending the Blue Suns to ambush him and Liara. While Feron searches the Broker's databases, Liara argues with the Broker, asking how he could trust the Collectors. The obscured figure is revealed to be a decoy that the Shadow Broker communicates through to his staff on Alingon. The Broker smugly explains that the exchange with the Collectors is underway. Feron then tells Liara he has the information they need. Liara smashes the decoy and destroys the room's equipment. As they head out to stop the exchange, Feron tells Liara who he is really working for.
evidence.for_key: Feron and the running of the Broker's agents

evidence.text: Feron, however, can't be released without killing him as he is hooked up to a torture machine that will fry his brain if tampered with. He tells the squad where to shut it off, and the squad sets off to free Feron and bring down the Shadow Broker once and for all. When they finally reach the Shadow Broker's office, they discover that the Broker is actually a yahg, a species that are effective outcasts in the galaxy. The Broker gloats about Liara's cluelessness, but she proves otherwise by deducing the yahg's lowly origins as the original Shadow Broker's "trophy" or even "pet". In a rage, the Broker throws his desk and engages Shepard and Liara in combat. After a protracted fight, in a coordinated effort, Shepard distracts the Broker while Liara brings down the liquid that was contained in the ceiling onto the Shadow Broker. The liquid causes the Broker's barrier to malfunction, and he dies in the subsequent explosion. As the squad pick themselves up, the power goes out briefly, allowing Feron to escape and make a break for the airlock. In the Broker's office, the Shadow Broker's agents start asking about the interruption in the signal. Liara walks over to the mass of computer banks, and after a few seconds, responds to the agents. In the Shadow Broker's artificially\-distorted voice, Liara fabricates a story that power went out temporarily when they were upgrading hardware. While this is happening, Feron storms into the office, brandishing his gun, but lowers it when he sees what is going on. Feron and Shepard ask if this is what Liara wants, and she is sure. Feron leaves to check on the power systems leaving Shepard and Liara alone. Liara assumes the position of Shadow Broker, with his minions none the wiser, and promises Shepard that she will turn the organization around. She also mentions she will be able to provide Shepard with more information now thanks to the Broker's extensive networks. She vows to use the Broker's resources for good; to help Shepard combat the Reapers. She and Feron remain on the Shadow Broker Base ship. Liara lets Shepard depart with the promise that they can return anytime. Shepard can also invite Liara aboard the Normandy for a tour of the ship and to catch up. If Shepard refuses to have Liara come aboard the Normandy, she sadly accepts the refusal. When walking away she stops to look at the Commander, only to have the Commander not return the glance. #### Romance “I spent two years mourning you. So if we're going to try this, I need to know you're always coming back.” During the Shadow Broker mission, Shepard has an opportunity to try and confront Liara about their relationship before boarding the Shadow Broker's ship while expressing resentment of Liara for using the Commander to help find the Shadow Broker. Liara responds that she can't "undo two years of mourning." After the yahg Broker's defeat and Liara's takeover of his job, Shepard questions whether this is what she wants. Liara begins enumerating the ways that her new position can benefit Shepard but bursts into tears afterwards, unbelieving that her two year quest for vengeance is over. If Shepard chooses to hug Liara, Shepard reassures her and they lightly kiss but Liara stops short. Liara implies they and their relationship have changed over the two years, but if Shepard interrupts her before she finishes, the Commander intimately holds her and they kiss deeply. Later, Shepard can ask Liara whether she ever developed a romantic relationship with Feron, but Liara assures Shepard that she and Feron are "just friends" and that Shepard made it clear to Feron that she was, as humans say, "taken." Alternatively, if Shepard opts not to take the kiss, she teasingly asks if Shepard is jealous and suggests that the Commander "do something about it." Liara misses Shepard but she doesn't want to put pressure on the Commander. Shepard has the option of just staying friends or becoming involved again. Regardless of the choice, Shepard invites Liara for a drink on the Normandy. Back in Shepard's cabin on the Normandy, Liara comments on the Normandy and mentions running into Joker. If Shepard is a male and in a relationship with Liara, Liara mentions that Joker asked her to record any parts of the conversation with the Commander where her eyes do that "freaky black eternity thing". If Shepard is a female, Liara relays Joker's interest in whether or not the two would be "acting out scenes from a vid called Vaenia." If the Commander chose to continue the romance, the conversation then focuses on Liara asking Shepard about their future. Shepard jokes about marrying, growing old and having lots of "little blue children".
evidence.for_key: Feron and the running of the Broker's agents

evidence.text: A momentary comm glitch from the battle causes the Broker's agents to radio his office asking for immediate updates on the situation. At first, Liara seems overwhelmed and unsure what to do. Then, she moves toward the panel and responds to the agents using the Shadow Broker's voice modification to avoid exposing herself: the situation is under control, and it was merely a hardware problem that disrupted communications. Liara ends the message by ordering all agents to resume standard procedures and to report an update on all operations within one solar day. Feron comes to the room and quickly pulls his pistol before he realizes everything has been dealt with. Liara explains that she is now the new Shadow Broker, believing that it is something she has to do. Feron leaves with the just\-revived other squadmate to check on the power system, leaving Liara and Shepard by themselves. Shepard can comfort a crying Liara with a hug, who is happy that her revenge is finally over after two years' worth of struggling. Liara thanks Shepard for what the Commander has helped her accomplish and assures that Shepard is welcome any time. The Shadow Broker's resources become available to Shepard. Feron stays with Liara to help around while he recovers. Along with everything else the former Broker owned, Liara assumes ownership of the yahg's Info Drone, which refers to any organic within its range as "Shadow Broker". In a subsequent conversation, Liara remarks that her role as the Shadow Broker will likely play key role in the upcoming war against the Reapers. She also provides Shepard with additional insight on the Shadow Broker's plans and what he knew. Shepard can ask her about Feron, who is now residing with Liara. Later, Shepard may choose to invite Liara to the Normandy for a catch up. On the other hand, if Shepard refuses to have Liara onboard the Normandy, she sadly accepts the refusal.
evidence.for_key: Feron and the running of the Broker's agents

evidence.text: “You pretend to be everywhere at once \-\- \-\- I already am! ” One month after the SSV Normandy's destruction, the General strikes a deal with the Shadow Broker for possession of Commander Shepard's body. The General is incensed at a delay in the transaction, caused by the emergence of the Illusive Man and Liara T'Soni who are also vying to retrieve it, but nonetheless is forced to accept the situation. The exchange eventually proceeds on the Broker's base on Alingon. The General sends a humanoid drone to the location, warning the Broker's underlings that the Collectors will not brook dishonesty or further delays. At first glance, the General thinks the body delivered is indeed Shepard's, and it praises the Broker for a job done well. However, one of the Broker's agents, Feron, claims the Broker now wants full payment upfront. The General refutes that it will pay half now and the other half when they've confirmed Shepard's identity personally, as per the original deal. The Collector General, transmitting directly to the Broker, accuses him of betrayal. The Broker counters that Feron, conspiring with Liara, severed his link to the base. Boasting that it is already everywhere compared to the Broker's pale imitation, the General has its on\-site drone relay to the Broker's enforcer Tazzik that Feron has betrayed their boss. The General scrambles to retrieve the body, but Liara successfully escapes the base with it. |  | ***“The chances of surviving are… slim.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 2** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |
evidence.for_key: Feron and the running of the Broker's agents

evidence.text: Liara rounds on Feron in the immediate aftermath of the failed retrieval, thinking he never really left the Broker's service despite earlier assurances. She gives Feron one last chance after hearing him claim it was an accident. They use Feron's ship, parked nearby, to pursue Tazzik. Liara complains about the standing room in Feron's cramped ship, though soon enough she has bigger problems on her plate. After arriving at the vicinity of Alingon, the Broker's automated sentries begin firing at Feron's ship. She wonders if the Broker actively attacks people working for him, though Feron just assures her the Broker doesn't like impromptu arrivals. When Feron threads the ship inside asteroids in order to lose the sentries, Liara quips the move wasn't really safe for them either. At the Broker's base on Alingon, Liara assesses the Broker's operation based on what she hears from Feron. She deems it inefficient, as the overly secretive procedures mean the Broker's agents keep stumbling over themselves. Feron deems it an advantage when he pretends to be on unscheduled Broker business with Liara as an "asari escort" to a pair of outside guards. Because of the constant referals to Shepard as merchandise, Liara begins to tire of hearing it when Feron explains the Alingon base's purpose to her. When they hear about Shepard's body arriving they discreetly tail a Collector going to see it. Liara springs into action again, but Feron once again advises restraint. Liara follows him to the Broker's sanctum, where he suspects they might get answers. Liara directly addresses the Broker at his command center, learning of his interest in Shepard's body as purely a business matter. She rejects the notion: aside from moral scruples, she posits instead that there may be a connection between the Reapers and the Collectors, where Shepard figures prominently in the puzzle. She moves to attack the Broker, but learns she is actually talking to a holoprojector. The Broker claims Tazzik has already finished the transaction. Angered, she biotically demolishes the entire command center. While in the throes of catharsis, Feron approaches her with a data stick containing a lot of the Broker's dealings. Liara thought the Collectors already have Shepard, but her hopes are rejuvenated when Feron says they're still at the north portal. She wants to move out, but Feron takes the moment to come clean with her.
evidence.for_key: Feron and the running of the Broker's agents

evidence.text: If Shepard assaulted the Shadow Broker's ship with Liara, Feron helps her abandon the base and save the valuable equipment when Cerberus attacks the ship. He then takes up a role as one of Liara's agents and takes control of Terminus operations, much to the dismay of Tazzik. He sends Shepard an e\-mail: **Info for you** --- Hi, Shepard: It's been a while. I'm glad to hear you made it off Earth and that Liara's with you. Getting off her old ship was the best thing we could've done. Can't tell you how sick I was of that cabin. And of tripping over that drone. I don't even know how it kept finding me in a ship that big, even after I turned off its tracking. I dug up some interesting information for you. Talk with Glyph to sort out the data. I hope it helps, Shepard. It's getting rough out there. \- Feron If Shepard didn't help Liara overthrow the Shadow Broker, then Liara will say that she had to hire dozens of mercenaries to storm the Broker's lair. Unfortunately, Feron didn't survive the assault.
evidence.for_key: Feron and the running of the Broker's agents

evidence.text: Liara single\-handedly defeats a squad of the Shadow Broker's guards. Feron catches up with her, but Liara shrugs him off, angry that he lied and has been a triple agent all along: his employer is Cerberus. He explains that he started out working for the Shadow Broker running small errands. Cerberus had been trying to recruit him repeatedly to gain a foothold in the Broker's operation. Feron only gave in to Cerberus when he learned that the Broker was working with the Collectors, and that the Collectors were interested in Commander Shepard's corpse. The Broker had become suspicious however, and was cutting Feron out of work. To get back in, Feron volunteered to steer Liara away from finding Shepard so he could retrieve Shepard himself. Feron also let Tazzik escape Omega so he had an excuse to return to Alingon and grab as much information about the Shadow Broker's dealings as he could. At the Alingon base's hangar, Liara and Feron watch as the Collector they saw earlier examines Shepard's body. Tazzik is ready to hand it over as soon as the Broker receives the promised payment. Feron boldly interrupts the scene, telling Tazzik that the Broker is unsatisfied with the current deal and wants all of the Collectors' payment now, before the body is exchanged. Tazzik believes him, and orders the body moved back into his ship's hold. Elsewhere, the Collector fumes to the Shadow Broker about this "betrayal". The Broker explains that Feron does not speak for him and is a traitor, but he can't communicate with Tazzik. Back in the hangar, the Collector alerts Tazzik, who pulls a gun on Feron. Liara hears Feron's signal and attacks the other guards and the Collector while Feron holds off Tazzik. Liara escapes on Tazzik's ship, but is forced to leave Feron behind. Sometime later at a Cerberus facility, Miranda and Liara watch as Cerberus doctors work on Commander Shepard's body. Liara suggests that bringing Shepard back may not be the right thing to do. Miranda expresses doubts that Shepard can be revived because the body was in worse condition than expected and the stasis container was of little help, but says the Illusive Man is more optimistic and willing to devote a considerable amount of resources toward the project. Liara leaves, realizing she has another friend to help now, and another enemy.
evidence.for_key: Feron and the running of the Broker's agents

evidence.text:
Tazzik was a salarian hitman employed by the Shadow Broker, unusually tall and rugged for a salarian, to the point that a Blue Suns krogan was surprised by his appearance.

In Mass Effect: Redemption, Tazzik arrived on Omega in 2183 to oversee the Blue Suns operation moving Commander Shepard's body for transport to the Collectors, and was recognized as a reputable Broker agent by Feron. Despite interference from Liara T'Soni, he escaped Omega with Shepard's body and brought it to the Broker's main base on Alingon. During the handover, Feron walked in claiming the Broker wanted full payment rather than half; Tazzik was ready to believe him and had ordered the body taken back when the Collector negotiator outed Feron as a traitor. Feron then signaled Liara, who attacked and escaped with Tazzik's ship and Shepard's body. Tazzik was last seen elbowing Feron to the ground and beating his face bloody.

In Mass Effect 3, if Liara saved Feron from the Shadow Broker, then following the destruction of the Shadow Broker Base in 2186 Liara tasked Feron with tracking Tazzik down. Displeased at taking orders from Feron, Tazzik nonetheless complied, acting as bodyguard for Feron and a group of Shadow Broker agents gathering intel across the Terminus Systems. He remained unaware that Liara was the new Shadow Broker, apparently assuming nothing had changed beyond Feron's status shifting from liability to asset.
evidence.for_key: Feron and the running of the Broker's agents

evidence.text:
Shadow Broker Agents were the rank-and-file soldiers of the Shadow Broker's private army, tasked with defending the Broker's interests. They were encountered by Commander Shepard, Liara T'Soni, and the squad during the mission to bring down the Shadow Broker, appearing on Illium and at the Broker's base on Hagalaz.

Agents were armed with the standard M-8 Avenger and could use Flashbang Grenades. They had moderate health, and on higher difficulty levels also carried light shielding. The Flashbang Grenade made them more dangerous than ordinary Troopers, as they used it to dislodge players from cover and strip shields; the recommended response was to move away from a landed grenade and have Shepard look away to avoid being blinded.
evidence.for_key: Feron and the running of the Broker's agents

evidence.page: Rekindling with Ashley, from Sarah's Grief to the Push on Earth
evidence.text: Rekindling with Ashley, from Sarah's Grief to the Push on Earth. 2186, across the Reaper War, from Ashley's return to the Normandy through the final assault on Earth the SSV Normandy SR-2 (Ashley's quarters, the Captain's Quarters), the Citadel, and the London FOB Once Ashley is aboard the Normandy, taking up the Starboard Observation Deck quarters formerly occupied by Samara, she says little unless Shepard is pursuing a relationship with her. She sends an email asking for help: her younger sister Sarah, newly widowed, doesn't want to face her grief alone, and Ashley wants to comfort her. Shepard's being comforting and respectful with Ashley over this cements the relationship further.
evidence.for_key: grief managed through information and surveillance

evidence.section: *07/06/2010 \- Containment of Vital Information More Difficult Than Ever*
evidence.text: *“The struggle to contain vital information is a key part of any war, but today it's more difficult than ever. Citizen reporters, aided by cheap, concealable technology such as camera\-clothing and micro\-surveillance can easily cross the line from witness to antiwar activist or spy. "We feed the major media outlets satisfying, nonvital info", said Lieutenant Colonel Sanex Irvinus. "In return, they tend to stay professional. It's more difficult when a noncombatant plants a microbug on a person or vehicle. Their data goes straight to the antiwar media, and minutes later, the mainstream echoes it. You wouldn't believe the counter\-surveillance methods we've had to use". Activist groups like TruthHax say the trend won't go away. "Intelligence services and media conglomorates pay for info, and activists just do it because it's right", said one unnamed source. "If you could stop a war with information, if you could kill its support without driving up the cost in lives, wouldn't you be obliged to try?"”*
evidence.for_key: grief managed through information and surveillance

evidence.text: By 2185, Liara has become an information broker on Illium. Due to her association with Shepard, the Illusive Man gathered intelligence on her and erroneously came to the conclusion that she has begun working for the Shadow Broker, blacklisting her from Shepard's prospective new team. Liara sponsors Shepard's docking fees while the Commander is on the planet, extending an invitation to meet up at her office. When they finally reunite after two years, however, Shepard receives a less than warm welcome. Liara is unable to talk to the Commander freely since all of her conversations are probably being recorded. Her personality has become much darker and ruthless, showing willingness to break the law and to threaten people in order to achieve success in the information trade. She even uses a quote her mother, Matriarch Benezia, once said when threatening a contact: "Have you faced an asari commando unit before? Few humans have..." Her change in personality is later revealed to be attributed to her hatred of the Shadow Broker and her determination to end him for the grief the Broker put her through. Shepard can try to break through her shell and see the real Liara, but only for a moment. If asked about her needs, Shepard offers to track down the Shadow Broker's agent known as the Observer. She is also willing to provide the Commander with information on the locations of some of the potential mission recruits.
evidence.for_key: grief managed through information and surveillance

Other information displayed here are health and shield stats as well as veteran bonuses, if any, and the toggles to set the character as a favorite in the app or as active in the game.

evidence.text: The room is located behind the Intel Center's main console, reachable through some stairs and a footway. It consists of a waiting lounge at one end and the archive itself on the other end. Feron relaxes on a sofa in the lounge, and ambient music in the room can be changed through a datapad at the table beside him. The archive is on a raised circular platform where videos are displayed on a screen and can be zoomed in if necessary. All surveillance footage have audio, but are unintelligible, requiring context cues to understand what's transpiring on the screen. The Broker's Info Drone identifies the videos as they are presented. Clips are presented in batches, with more revealed in subsequent visits to the archive.

evidence.text: A badly\-wounded Tali'Zorah nar Rayya stumbled upon Dr. Michel's clinic in the Upper Wards and collapsed in her arms. The doctor helped Tali into a corner and while treating her wounds became an audience for the quarian's tale of her journey and woes. Tali had obtained information linking Saren Arterius to the geth, and she was pursued by the Spectre's lackeys all the way to the Citadel to stop her from exposing it. Tali managed to defeat the most tenacious pursuer but was shot along the way, which led to her limping to the clinic. As she finished the story, Dr. Michel assured her that she's safe for the moment. A volus nearby was also listening to the quarian's story and mentioned that he is an information broker: he can contact the Shadow Broker to ensure that Tali's information can reach the right people. With this, Dr. Michel encouraged Tali to trust the volus. |  | ***“This mission just got a lot more complicated.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.text: Liselle was a daughter of Aria T'Loak and the lover of Paul Grayson. When Grayson began working for Aria under the alias Paul Johnson, Aria, unable to find any information on his past, ordered Liselle to kill him; instead Liselle pleaded for his life, arguing he was useful and loyal, and later became his lover. She was part of the team Aria sent to secure a shipment of red sand from the Talons, a turian mercenary gang, and did not object when Grayson had the sand stashed in his apartment. Visiting Grayson's apartment after his call, the two were attacked by Grayson's former employers, Cerberus. Liselle was hit with a tranquilizer dart and knocked unconscious, and Kai Leng then killed her by slitting her throat with a kitchen knife, leaving her to bleed out on Grayson's bed, where Aria later found her. The small dart wound was overlooked against the neck injury, leading Aria to suspect Grayson had killed her, and her grief and fury drove her to seek revenge. These events occurred in Mass Effect: Retribution.

evidence.text:
Kolyat Krios was the drell son of Thane and Irikah Krios. As described in Mass Effect: Foundation, Thane proclaimed him a gift from Arashu at birth but was an absent, clueless parent; Kolyat was raised by Irikah while Thane's freelance assassination jobs grew longer and farther away. When Thane's enemies attacked, Kolyat hid on his mother's instruction and was never found, but never saw Irikah alive again. He witnessed Thane's grief and breakdown while in the custody of crime scene investigators.

In Mass Effect 2, Thane had stored money with volus bankers on the Citadel as Kolyat's inheritance, but Kolyat took it early and became a hitman. Hired by Elias Kelham through information from Mouse, he was contracted to assassinate the turian politician Joram Talid in the 800 Blocks. Commander Shepard and Thane tracked Talid from separate positions to stop Kolyat from becoming a killer. If they failed to coordinate, Kolyat killed Talid and escaped; otherwise Shepard interrupted him and, with Thane, stopped the execution. Kolyat, furious at Thane's lifelong absence, calmed as his father explained why Irikah was killed and why he could not return, and called Kolyat the only good thing he ever added to the world. In the C-Sec interrogation room Kolyat could face community service, work for Captain Bailey, or go to trial; Thane stayed in contact either way.

In Mass Effect 3, if reconciled, the two remained in contact. Kolyat appeared at Thane's side after Kai Leng mortally wounded Thane during the Cerberus attack on the Citadel; despite a blood transfusion, Kepral's Syndrome made recovery impossible. At Thane's deathbed, Kolyat finished his father's prayer to Kalahira, having spent the past year with the drell priests, and led a prayer for redemption that Thane revealed was intended for Shepard. In the Citadel DLC, Kolyat emailed Shepard requesting a memorial service, held at Shepard's apartment with Thane's old crewmates and the salarian Councilor. He planned to lobby the Councilor (Valern or Esheel) to fund salarian research into Kepral's Syndrome, and told Shepard he had found three intercepted video messages from Thane addressed to the Commander.

evidence.text:
The Video Archive was a chamber in the Shadow Broker Base where the Shadow Broker kept archived surveillance clips of observed people across the galaxy. After Liara T'Soni's takeover of the base, Commander Shepard could view the footage freely. The room lay behind the Intel Center's main console, with a waiting lounge where Feron relaxed on a sofa (ambient music adjustable via a datapad) and a raised circular platform displaying the clips. All footage had audio but was unintelligible, so the Broker's Info Drone identified each clip, which were revealed in batches over successive visits.

The clips showed brief, often incriminating or comic moments: Aria T'Loak overseeing a Blue Suns execution and in her Afterlife booth; Emily Wong dancing and interviewing amid burning hovercars; Donnel Udina shoving a C-Sec agent and watching an Afterlife dancer; Captain Armando Bailey drinking by a window and leaving the Zakera Cafe armed; David Anderson meeting a Cerberus agent and punching Udina in the stomach; Captain Preitor Gavorn killing vorcha and fleeing gunfire; Khalisah al-Jilani punched by a krogan, kicked by a volus, and kissing an asari; Matriarch Aethyta viewing a photo of Liara, attacking a volus with biotics, and headbutting a krogan; Jacob Taylor doing shirtless sit-ups; Legion boarding the Derelict Reaper; Garrus attacking mercs; a Keeper disposing of a surveillance camera; Jack leveling Blue Suns mercs during her escape; Thane Krios killing a mercenary on Kahje then shooting the camera; Fred Mazzei witnessing a hit; Urdnot Torsk shoving a salarian into the varren pit and executing a human with Fortack; Grunt punching an Eclipse Trooper; and Samara ensnaring a fleeing merc's hovercar with biotics. At least three additional videos, said to depict Detective Anaya on Illium, Tali'Zorah on Haestrom, and Mordin Solus on Sur'Kesh, were cut during development.
